declaration.preface: Integrity is the foundation on which Shilpa Medicare Limited has built its reputation over more than three decades. We recognize that sustainable business success in the highly regulated, patient-critical pharmaceutical industry demands more than technical excellence. It demands that every business decision, relationship, transaction, and communication be conducted with absolute honesty, transparency, and accountability.
declaration.declaration: This Corporate Governance Policy establishes the ethical standards and behavioral expectations that govern how SML conducts business across all its operations, geographies, and relationships. It covers seven core business ethics areas: Corruption & Bribery Prevention; Fraud Prevention; Conflict of Interest; Information Security & Confidentiality; Anti-Money Laundering; Ethical Marketing; and Third-Party Management.
declaration.scope:
This Policy applies to all operations of Shilpa Medicare Limited and its group entities, Subsidiaries, Joint Ventures including API manufacturing facilities, formulation plants, R&D centers, CDMO operations, biologics units, corporate and administrative offices, and all associated with Shilpa Medicare Operational Locations. The Policy also extends to all global sales offices located in Malaysia, Austria, Dubai (UAE), the United Kingdom, Spain, and the United States of America.

It is applicable to all employees (permanent and contract), management, directors, business associates, vendors, contractors, and all internal and external stake holders working on behalf of the Company

Corruption & Bribery Prevention: We maintain absolute zero tolerance for bribery and corruption in any form whether direct or indirect, cash or in-kind, domestic or international across all business activities, geographies, and stakeholder relationships, in full compliance with the Prevention of Corruption Act 1988, the Companies Act 2013, FCPA, and the UK Bribery Act 2010.
We ensure full transparency in gifts, hospitality, and donations by maintaining an updated Gift & Hospitality Register and enforcing defined approval and documentation procedures.
We promote a culture of ethical decision-making by encouraging employees to report concerns without fear through established reporting channels.

The Company maintains an effective Anti-Bribery and Corruption (ABC) management system by conducting periodic risk assessments, internal audits, and management reviews aligned with ISO 37001 principles.
Facilitation payments regardless of amount, local practice, or perceived necessity are strictly prohibited across all SML operations and geographies without exception.

We will maintain an Anti-Bribery and Corruption (ABC) program comprising annual training, risk assessments, periodic control testing, and management reporting, aligned with ISO 37001 Anti-Bribery Management System principles.
Fraud Prevention: We are committed to the prevention, detection, and investigation of all forms of fraud including financial statement misrepresentation, procurement fraud, expense claim fraud, asset misappropriation, payroll fraud, regulatory data falsification, and identity fraud.
We aim to increase employee awareness of fraud risks by conducting regular training and communication programs.
We aim to ensure accurate and transparent record-keeping across the Company by maintaining complete and up-to-date documentation for all transactions.

We aim to prevent and detect fraudulent activities across all operations by maintaining robust internal controls, including segregation of duties, dual authorization for transactions, independent reconciliations, and periodic internal audits across all entities and financial processes.

We aim to ensure timely reporting of suspected fraudulent activities by requiring all employees to report concerns through a confidential whistleblower mechanism, with protection against any adverse consequences for good-faith reporting.

We will conduct periodic fraud risk assessments across high-risk functions including procurement, finance, sales, and regulatory affairs and implement targeted controls to address identified vulnerabilities.
Conflict of Interest: We strive to eliminate risks arising from conflicts of interest across the Company by promoting independent and objective decision-making in all roles.

All employees must complete an annual Conflict of Interest Declaration covering outside employment, directorships, financial interests in suppliers or customers, family relationships with business counterparties, and membership of regulatory advisory bodies.

We establish and maintain a structured and comprehensive framework for the identification, disclosure, and evaluation of potential conflicts of interest through periodic declarations and systematic review mechanisms.
We enhance employee awareness and understanding of conflict of interest risks and expectations through regular communication, targeted training programs, and accessible guidance materials.
We promote early identification of conflicts in sensitive functions by requiring proactive reporting from employees involved in procurement, regulatory, clinical, and financial activities.
Where a conflict of interest is confirmed, the affected employee will be recused from the relevant decision or process. Recusal decisions and management actions will be documented and retained.
Information Security & Confidentiality: We are committed to protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of all business-critical information including API synthesis routes, formulation data, clinical trial results, regulatory dossiers, financial records, employee data, and customer information from unauthorized access, disclosure, modification, or destruction.

All employees handling confidential or sensitive information maintains and adhere to SML's Information Security Policy, data classification guidelines, and applicable data protection laws including the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 (India) and GDPR requirements for EU operations.

Access to confidential systems and data will be granted on a need-to-know basis, with role-based access controls, multi-factor authentication, and regular access reviews enforced across all SML IT environments.
We strengthen endpoint and network security across all operations by deploying firewalls, antivirus solutions, endpoint detection and response (EDR), and secure network configurations.
We enhance employee awareness on cybersecurity risks and practices by conducting regular training on phishing, data protection, and secure system usage.
We manage third-party information security risks effectively by conducting due diligence, enforcing security clauses in contracts, and monitoring vendor compliance.
All employees, contractors, and third parties with access to SML's confidential information must sign Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) before being granted access.
Anti-Money Laundering: We are committed to full compliance with the Prevention of Money Laundering Act 2002 (PMLA), FEMA, and applicable international AML standards, ensuring that its financial transactions, business relationships, and commercial operations are not used to facilitate money laundering, terrorist financing, or other financial crimes.

Know Your Customer (KYC) verification and due diligence will be conducted for all new business relationships including distributors, agents, export partners, and significant new customers before commercial engagement commences.
We will not accept, process, or facilitate cash payments or transactions structured to circumvent reporting thresholds or regulatory requirements under any circumstances.

We strengthen ongoing monitoring of financial transactions and business relationships by implementing transaction screening and periodic review mechanisms to identify unusual or suspicious activities.
We reinforce employee awareness and accountability toward AML compliance by conducting regular training on red flags, reporting obligations, and regulatory expectations.
Ethical Marketing: All promotional, scientific, medical, and commercial communications for SML's APIs, formulations, biologicals, and CDMO services must be accurate, balanced, evidence-based, and fully compliant with applicable regulations including CDSCO requirements, UCPMP guidelines, WHO ethical criteria for pharmaceutical promotion.

No exaggerated, misleading, unsubstantiated, or off-label claims will be made in any marketing material, regulatory submission, scientific publication, or customer communication, regardless of the market or channel.

All promotional materials and digital communications will undergo mandatory review and approval by the Medical, Regulatory, and Legal functions before release, ensuring factual accuracy and regulatory compliance.
Third-Party Management: All third parties including raw material suppliers, contract manufacturers, logistics partners, distributors, agents, consultants, and technology vendors are expected to comply with SML's Corporate Governance Policy and the principles of the PSCI Code of Conduct.

Pre-engagement due diligence encompassing business ethics, anti-corruption, financial crime risk, legal compliance, and reputational screening will be conducted for all new third-party relationships before any commercial engagement commences.
All third-party agreements will include mandatory ethics, anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and data protection compliance clauses, with contractual rights for SML to audit third-party compliance.

responsibilities.duty: Approve and endorse the Corporate Governance Policy and overall ethics and compliance strategy, ensuring integration with SML's business strategy.
Provide visible and sustained leadership commitment to a culture of integrity, transparency, and zero tolerance for corruption, fraud, and misconduct.
Ensure adequate financial, human, and organizational resources are available for effective implementation and monitoring of business ethics programs.

responsibilities.role: Board of Directors & Ethics & Compliance Committee
responsibilities.duty: Provide Board-level oversight of SML's business ethics, anti-corruption, and compliance programs, reviewing material violations, systemic risks, and annual performance against Policy targets.

responsibilities.role: Board of Directors & Ethics & Compliance Committee
responsibilities.duty: Review and approve material updates to the Corporate Governance Policy and related frameworks, procedures, and enforcement standards.
Own Policy implementation, compliance monitoring, investigation management, and performance reporting across all SML entities.
Lead the Ethics & Compliance program including anti-bribery risk assessments, conflict-of-interest management, AML screening, and third-party due diligence.
Review and update the Policy at least annually, or when triggered by legislative changes, enforcement developments, or material incidents.
Monitor applicable anti-corruption, fraud, data protection, marketing ethics, and AML legislative and regulatory developments affecting SML's operations globally.
Provide legal guidance on Policy compliance, investigation procedures, enforcement actions, and regulatory disclosure obligations.
Maintain and enforce the financial controls - including segregation of duties, dual authorization, and independent reconciliation - that prevent and detect fraud and financial misconduct.
Conduct periodic internal compliance and fraud risk audits across all entities.
Embed ethics and compliance expectations into the employee lifecycle - from recruitment and induction through performance management, promotions, and exits.
Administer disciplinary proceedings for ethics violations in coordination with the CCO and Legal, ensuring fair process and documented outcomes.
Comply with this Policy and all related compliance procedures, codes of conduct, and training requirements at all times.
Exercise ethical judgment in all business decisions, and seek guidance from the Compliance team when facing ethical uncertainties.
Report suspected ethics violations, policy breaches, or compliance concerns through designated channels.

policy.monitoring:
Shilpa Medicare Limited is committed to the continuous strengthening of its business ethics and compliance performance across all operations, geographies, and business relationships.

Anti-corruption training completion, third-party compliance scores, conflict-of-interest register updates, gifts & hospitality log reviews, data breach incidents, marketing compliance audits, and AML screening outcomes are tracked at each entity on a regular basis.

Periodic internal compliance audits and independent ethics assessments evaluate adherence to Policy requirements, identify control gaps, and verify progress against targets across all issue areas.

All reported ethics violations, suspected fraud, conflicts of interest, data security incidents, and policy non-compliances are investigated, root-cause analyzed, and closed through the CAPA system within defined timelines.

Business ethics and compliance performance covering all seven issue areas is reviewed by the Ethics & Compliance Committee and Senior Management at least quarterly.

Business ethics performance data is compiled and disclosed in SML's annual BRSR under SEBI LODR Regulations, and in applicable statutory filings under the Companies Act 2013.
policy.reviewMechanism: This Corporate Governance Policy is reviewed at least once every year, or whenever triggered by significant changes in business operations, new or amended applicable legislation, changes in regulatory requirements, significant ethics incidents, or material stakeholder concerns. The review is conducted by the Chief Compliance Officer in consultation with Senior Management, the Legal team, and the Ethics & Compliance Committee.
